summary.text: 备 is the simplified form corresponding to 備, a graph interpreted as a person carrying an arrow container—a scene associated with readiness. Its current meanings include “prepare” and “ready.”

formation.text: 備 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 人 depicts a person, while 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container and is also assigned a sound role. Read together, the graph has been interpreted as a person carrying a quiver, linking the image with preparedness. The proposed sound role is not independently confirmed by a historical reading for 𤰈. The simplified graph 备 corresponds to 備 in the 1956 scheme.

components.text: In 備, 人 depicts the person in the interpreted carrying scene associated with preparedness.
In 備, 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container, identified in texts as a quiver. It is also assigned a sound role, though a historical reading for 𤰈 is not independently confirmed.

sound_limitation.text: The supplied evidence gives no independently verified, character-specific historical reading for 𤰈. 備 has historical readings, but these do not establish 𤰈’s reading or verify its sound role.

components.text: 备 is the officially adopted simplified form corresponding to 備. A secondary account proposes a route through the variant 俻, but the official scheme does not establish that derivation.

history.text: 備 appears in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, but its earliest appearance is not dated here.

The right-hand component is printed as 𤰇 in some forms and described as a change from seal-script 𤰈. In bronze forms, its lower part is also reported to change to 用, tentatively proposed as a sound element. These accounts do not establish a complete dated sequence.
The 1956 simplification scheme lists 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 was separately recognized as a variant of 備, but the scheme does not identify it as the direct source of 备.

uncertainties.text: The carrying-quiver interpretation links the graph with preparedness but does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. Texts identify the pictured container as 箙, and 備 is reported as writing 箙 in a bronze inscription; neither establishes the pictured object’s original name or proves a sound match between that name and 𤰈.

備 has recorded glosses including prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these meanings.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver scene may help explain preparedness, but does not prove the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss 慎也 means “cautious” or “careful”; it does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.

A bronze inscription reportedly uses 備 as a written sign for 箙, “quiver,” a different word. This proposed phonetic borrowing would depend on similarity between the words’ pronunciations; the evidence here does not verify that resemblance. Nor does the loan establish the pictured object’s original name or pronunciation.

overview.text: 備 is interpreted as a person carrying a quiver, a scene associated with being equipped and ready. The 1956 scheme adopted 备 as the simplified form corresponding to 備; today it commonly means “prepare” or “ready.”
